newsitem.title: USA: U.S. disinflation, bond ranges to continue - PIMCO.
newsitem.headline: U.S. disinflation, bond ranges to continue - PIMCO.

text.p: Founder and Managing Director of Pacific Investment Management Co (PIMCO) William Gross said on Wednesday he will continue to invest following a model of disinflation and a rangebound bond market to the turn of the century.

Gross outlined his strategies at the Fixed-Income Analysts Society Inc's 17th annual bond conference in New York, at which he was one of two investment professionals inducted to the FIASI Hall of Fame.
Late Goldman, Sachs & Co partner Fischer Black was posthumously inducted to the FIASI Hall of Fame.

Gross said expectations for steady to lower inflation are based on improvements in global trade that keep wages low. That, in turn, has reinvigorated capital markets, which will be vigilant in moving funds away from markets that "misbehave."

The period of disinflation began with Paul Volcker's hard money policy in 1981, Gross said, and the bond market has essentially mirrored the phenomenon. But he added there could be low inflation that could be detrimental.
"I would have to realize at some point there's not much more juice in this orange to squeeze," he said.
